added_claims.speaker: Geoffrey Garrett
added_claims.quote: if we then in a like a two decade period do away with uh internal combustion engines, that'd be pretty amazing.
added_claims.claim: Garrett sees a possible phase-out of the internal combustion engine, the defining technology of the 20th century, within about two decades, a structural shift for autos, oil demand and metals supply chains.
added_claims.indicator: EV share of new car sales
added_claims.direction: ICE and oil demand down; battery metals demand up
added_claims.conditions: EV adoption continues at policy-driven pace

corrections.issue: Mixed speakers: Tangen explains Norway's subsidies, charging network, taxi-lane access and no annual fees; the point that the US is a fossil-fuel exporter with the world's cheapest petrol, making EVs harder there, is Garrett's.
corrections.fix: Nicolai Tangen: Norway reached about 90% EV share of new car sales through large subsidies, a nationwide charging network, taxi-lane access and no annual fees, so buying a combustion car made no economic sense. Garrett adds that cheap petrol in the US (a fossil-fuel exporter) makes the same logic harder there.

completeness_estimate: 0.95 - interview is mostly leadership and business-education talk with no macro content; first reader caught nearly all the trade, EV and AI points, missing only the ICE phase-out remark; one speaker mix-up.
